gen-fs-stardom-gf-cascadia-code: Razor-thin hairlines hang off fat, thick diagonal stems in Stardom, and the lowercase is oversized to match. Cascadia Code answers in a plain sans with a wire-like skeleton, so a larger heading over a modest body should look right.
gen-fs-stardom-gf-cascadia-mono: Loud, swaggering, and slightly theatrical, Stardom swings from heavy strokes to hair-thin lines. And Cascadia Mono follows in sans-serif, its curves as thick as its stems, like tracing a single thread beneath the show.
gen-fs-stardom-gf-lexend-exa: Big-lunged and theatrical, Stardom lurches between fat stems and hairlines in every letter it draws. Lexend Exa takes over below with a stubby, wide-open sans that reads steadily.
gen-fs-stardom-gf-lexend-mega: Fat stems, fine hairlines, big drama. Lexend Mega sits below in a plain sans with no hairlines anywhere, and a tall body height close to the capitals, so a generous heading size against a modest body would let each keep its own voice.
gen-fs-stardom-gf-lexend-peta: Stardom swells its curves and joins them with hairlines, a showy, high-contrast look that fills a line fast. Lexend Peta does the quiet work, crossbars matching stems.
gen-fs-stardom-gf-lexend-zetta: Thick stems crossed by paper-thin strokes give Stardom its dramatic, swollen-and-sliced look. And Lexend Zetta, a sans-serif of constant-width ribbon strokes and widely tracked letters, gives the page somewhere to rest after the spectacle.
gen-fs-stardom-gf-montserrat-alternates: Chunky stems with fine threads attached: that is Stardom, loud and theatrical. And Montserrat Alternates, a plain sans cut to one stroke width, keeps long lines of text steady, its lowercase crowding up toward the capital line.
gen-fs-styro-gf-aldrich: Styro packs its letters in tight, almost crowded. Aldrich, a sans with a tall x-height and open, cupped rounds, lets a long page unroll like following one thick thread.
gen-fs-styro-gf-amiko: Styro has a retro, commanding swagger, its oversized lowercase pressed close with barely a gap in the e and c. Amiko, a plain sans, flares its terminals outward and lets the text breathe.
gen-fs-styro-gf-anek-bangla: Styro crowds its sizable lowercase tight, closing up every letter until the line feels pressed and retro. Anek Bangla, a plain sans, opens its wide s curves and keeps ascenders short.
